added_failures_note: Derived from the reviewed run's own two suite logs. logs/suite-base.log (d5da568f, base product files, completed to '13 failed, 8539 passed, 11 skipped' at 08:46) and logs/suite-head.log (8b1643981, completed to '3 failed, 8549 passed, 11 skipped' at 08:46) are compared id by id: head fails test_anchor_ab_aggregate.py::test_population_derived_from_selection, test_anchor_ab_aggregate.py::test_verdict_computed_from_conditions and test_dd_gap_automated_writers.py::test_review_writer_requires_successful_owned_transition[None-name]; the base arm carries the latter two plus eleven more. So exactly one head id is absent from the base arm. That id is load-sensitive under -n 8: the same file is 13 passed in isolation at head (logs/gate-head.log second run), so it is not a regression this change causes, but it is an added id against the stated base and the manifest's 'adds no failure id' claim is therefore not literally met.

findings.text: `assert _selects(_claim_seed_cypher(), sources) == _selects(count_clause, sources)` is close to tautological. `_selects` decides only from the substrings 'FROM_DD_PATH' and 'PRODUCED_NAME', and the claim seed statement contains both regardless of the shared predicate -- 'MATCH (sns)-[:FROM_DD_PATH]->(imas0:IMASNode)' is its own pre-existing match and the predicate supplies PRODUCED_NAME -- so this line would stay true if the predicate stopped being applied to the seed. The independent guard for the claim side is tests/standard_names/test_drained_queue_exit.py:236, which compares the predicate text itself; this line adds no condition under which it would redden that line 236 does not already cover.

The `dd_path_bound` keyword on the new predicate has no caller. Every interpolated site -- graph_cost_and_claims.py:486, 506, 518, 530, cli/sn.py:619 and graph_parent_lifecycle.py:118 -- passes the default False, including the three claim statements that already carry `MATCH (sns)-[:FROM_DD_PATH]->...` a few lines below and so now test the same edge twice. The parameter is dead as shipped; either it should be used at the sites whose docstring rationale describes it, or it should not exist.

The head gate log carries no revision header, no command line and no trailing `EXIT=` line, and it concatenates two separate pytest runs (19 passed for test_frozen_stage_pool_guard.py + test_drained_queue_exit.py, then 13 passed for test_anchor_ab_aggregate.py) with no separator naming either. The manifest's `tests:` line names only test_drained_queue_exit.py, so the log cannot be tied to the command it claims and its exit status cannot be read from the file the way the manifest contract requires.

The declared negative control ran the six-test revision of the test file (07:23) and its failure list names `test_the_generate_count_mirrors_the_claim_seed_predicate`, a test that does not exist at the reviewed head; the delivered file has eight tests and two of them use `source_claim_predicate`, which does not exist at the base revision. A later and complete red-on-base receipt does exist -- logs/suite-base.log runs the head test files against the base product files and reddens 7 of the 8, all except the deliberately-passing `test_a_stuck_claim_still_reports_stalled_and_exits_one` -- but the field the manifest points at cannot be re-read against the delivered tests.

The checkpoint states `tests/standard_names adds no failure id against the base`, but the two suite logs it cites differ by one id: tests/standard_names/test_anchor_ab_aggregate.py::test_population_derived_from_selection fails at head and does not fail at base. The manifest's own failure_attribution explains it as a load flake that passes 13/13 in isolation at head, which is credible against logs/gate-head.log, but the stated comparison is contradicted by the receipts and the added-failure figure for this node is 1, not 0.

The landed evidence fragment is text-only although docs/figures/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-drained-queue-exit was a granted write path. The comparison the fragment rests on -- 104 pending sources, all 104 without a FROM_DD_PATH, beside 9,078 of 10,141 that carry one -- is exactly the shape a small bar or a two-state queue diagram carries better than a paragraph, and the user-global graphics mandate makes the figure the default for an evidence record of this kind.

The gate log records 19 passed over that file and test_frozen_stage_pool_guard.py; the tests do drive the real _compute_pool_progress count and the real _idle_exhaustion_watchdog and assert 'no_eligible_work' + exit 0 for the drained case (line 173) and 'stalled' + SystemExit(1) for a claimable source (line 180); the seven modified Cypher statements were EXPLAINed against the live graph, 7 of 7 ok (logs/explain.log). item_verdicts.goal: The goal is to make a drained SN run exit cleanly instead of reporting a deadlock when only unclaimable sources remain pending. The diff defines that claimability once at imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_foundation.py:201 and reads it from all six claim guard sites (graph_cost_and_claims.py:486/506/518/530), the CLI count the run watchdog reads (imas_codex/cli/sn.py:619, fed by _pool_pending_fn at sn.py:1012 and :1142) and the exported count (graph_parent_lifecycle.py:118), so pending work is now work a pool can select.

justifications.durability: logs/suite-base.log runs the delivered test file against the base product files and reddens 7 of its 8 tests (test_drained_queue_exit.py:156, 161, 167, 173, 189, 212, 226), so the guards do fail when the change is reverted; the one weak line is the claim-side comparison at test_drained_queue_exit.py:223, which is satisfied by the seed statement's pre-existing FROM_DD_PATH match and would survive a predicate regression.
justifications.evidence: logs/suite-head.log and logs/suite-base.log are complete with headers and summary lines and logs/explain.log records 7 of 7 EXPLAIN ok, but the head gate log has no revision header or EXIT line, the declared negative control predates the delivered test file, and one added failure id contradicts the manifest's 'adds no failure id' claim.
